Answers the socle v0.50.0 finding relayed to this repository: `ci.yml` built the same instrumented tree twice on every pull request, because the shared check runs `make asan-ubsan` and this repository's own `sanitizers` job ran it too.

**A third way, and the reason for it.** The two options offered each delete a required status check of `main`: `sanitizer_command: ""` removes `check / sanitizers`, deleting our job removes `sanitizers`. Both are in the protection of this branch, and a required context that stops being produced locks the default branch. That is the trap this repository walked into two days ago with the `ubuntu-24.04` legs. So the work is split instead of moved:

| Sanitizer | Runs where, after this change |
|---|---|
| ASan and UBSan, Linux | the socle's shared job, green today |
| TSan and static analyzer, Linux | this repository's `sanitizers` job |
| ASan, UBSan, TSan, mutants, macOS | this repository's `macos-gates` |

No coverage is lost, no job is renamed, both required contexts keep reporting, and the protection of `main` needs no edit.

**Socle adopted to 0.50.0** in this same commit rather than a pull request of its own, as the conventions ask. Its check legs are unchanged from 0.41.0, so nothing is renamed.

**Two notes back to the socle.** Its detector matches the text of a command, not the host it runs on, so after this change it still reports five lines: our Linux TSan, which the shared job never runs, and the four steps of `macos-gates`, which run on macOS while the shared job is Linux-only. A product that sanitizes on macOS cannot duplicate a Linux job. And on the billing motive: this repository is public, so its GitHub-hosted minutes are free and its duplicate contributed nothing to the organisation's overage. It was still waste, and it delayed every pull request, which is why it is fixed here.

Verified: `maelys-release check` at v0.50.0 gives both verdicts ok; `make clean check` passes; `actionlint` clean on both workflows; `git diff --check` clean. No library code changes.

body.body:
**Essai, à ne pas fusionner.** Candidat `460dd8e` du socle (futur v0.40.0).

Le candidat fait que `cut` **audite sa propre écriture avant de créer une
branche** : il prend le dernier commit qui a déplacé `VERSION`, en tire les
fichiers dont le diff retirait l'ancienne version et ajoutait la nouvelle, et
exige que cette coupe-ci ait déplacé la version dans les mêmes.

**Pourquoi cet essai est chez vous.** maelys-system est l'un des deux produits
que la mesure désigne comme exposés : votre bump `0.9.0 -> 0.9.1` a déplacé la
version dans `include/maelys/sys/version.h` en plus de `VERSION`, et
`maelys-release.conf` ne déclare pas `[cut] after-version`. Avec le socle
actuel, votre prochaine `cut` écrirait `VERSION` seul, pousserait la branche,
ouvrirait la PR — et `make check-version`, que votre `make check` exécute,
la refuserait là.

Avec ce candidat, le plan vous le dit **avant toute écriture**, et `--apply`
refuse avant qu'une branche existe, en nommant le fichier.

**Ce que cet essai exerce ici :** le diff produit est vide hors le sha du pin
(vérifié en adoptant le même produit depuis `v0.39.0` et depuis le candidat),
donc il vérifie que la bascule passe votre CI et que `check` reste vert.

**Ce qu'il n'exerce pas :** `cut` lui-même, qui tourne sur la machine de
l'opérateur et non dans la CI. Il a été passé à la main sur un clone de
maelys-egress — refus correct, `VERSION` restauré, aucune branche créée — et
en plan sur maelys-cli et maelys-json, qui déclarent `after-version` et ne
reçoivent donc aucun avertissement.

Une source apt tierce de l'image du runner GitHub a servi un index incohérent aujourd'hui, et tous les jobs Linux qui faisaient `apt-get update && apt-get install` sont passés au rouge — dans ce dépôt comme ailleurs dans la flotte, pour une raison qu'aucun produit ne contrôle.

```
E: Failed to fetch https://dl.google.com/linux/chrome-stable/deb/dists/stable/main/binary-amd64/Packages.gz  Hash Sum mismatch
##[error]Process completed with exit code 100.
```

L'`update` devient donc best-effort et rapporte un avertissement ; l'installation qui suit décide. **Un paquet manquant fait toujours échouer le job**, bruyamment : c'est l'installation qui a besoin de l'archive, pas le rafraîchissement d'un index que ce dépôt n'utilise pas.

Les paquets installés ici viennent tous de l'archive Ubuntu, jamais d'une source tierce de l'image, donc la résilience ajoutée ne masque aucune dépendance réelle.

Le socle a pris la même forme dans ses propres workflows en v0.22.1, et cela a suffi à rendre ses jobs verts pendant que la panne durait. Cette PR l'applique aux workflows que ce dépôt possède, que le socle ne régénère pas.

Changement mécanique, vérifié par `actionlint`.

**Kept from the proposal**
- Both parents of a publication opened first (final link followed) and anchored by descriptor: `renameat2` / `renameatx_np` and the parent sync run through them, so replacing either path after the open redirects nothing. Test: a relinked parent directory during the rename.
- `fchmod(0600)` on the inode before any failure path of `write_exclusive`.
- Checkout headers before consumer `CPPFLAGS` in every rule, proven by `scripts/include-precedence-check.sh` in `make check`.

**Dropped from the proposal**
- The `.maelys-publish-*` quarantine: a crash between its two renames left the object orphaned, staging and destination absent (S-01), a permanent `verify` error in oci's blob directory (S-07), plus a surviving mutant (S-03). There are two states after the call, staging or destination, a crash included; the type-check/rename window is named in the contract.

- `O_NOCTTY` in `open_plain` (S-04).
- Reset seen from the sending side is `ERR_RESET` on both hosts (S-05): `SO_ERROR` read where macOS answers `EPIPE` or HUP without WRITE; then `ERR_CLOSED`. Test in both paths, both hosts.

body.body:
The four reactor defects of the 0.8.0 cold audit and the small findings, with tests. No new surface; ABI 1 unchanged.

- **Id collision**: a watch id and a timer id could be numerically equal; `timer_cancel(loop, watch)` cancelled an unrelated timer. Ids now carry a kind bit (bit 63) above a 31-bit generation; the wrong kind is `ERR_NOT_FOUND`. Test in `test_sys.c`.
- **Closed before unwatch**: on epoll, `unwatch` failed with EBADF and left the slot and the descriptor number blocked forever (`ERR_STATE` on every later watch of that number); kqueue and poll answered differently. `unwatch` now releases the registration when the backend reports ENOENT or EBADF and returns OK; loop.h says a surviving dup keeps the epoll registration alive. Test in `test_backends.c`.
- **Starvation**: with a caller array smaller than the ready set, poll reported the same first entries forever. Two changes: the loop asks the backend for exactly the caller's capacity (the kernel rotates its ready list on what was reported, so the extra slot for the wakeup made epoll and kqueue starve too once the array was full), and the poll backend reports from a rotating cursor with the wakeup entry always examined. The wake fits by construction now; the "consumed when full" guard became dead code and is removed with its mutant (18/18). Fairness test on every backend: four ready, capacity two, all four within two steps.
- **HUP and ERROR**: written as the hosts allow. HUP is promised with READ; for WRITE-only watches the hosts disagree and nothing is promised; ERROR is an indication (a reset is READ|HUP|ERROR on Linux and now on kqueue, READ|HUP on macOS poll). `test_backends.c` freezes the three scenarios per host with a real TCP reset.
- Small: `directory_sync` follows a final link (`/tmp` on macOS) and `sync_parent` calls it; `deadline_after` cannot return the INFINITE sentinel; `connect_start` writes `*out_state` on OK only; SIGPIPE after `detach` on Linux documented; regular files named as not watchable.

body.body:
The file primitives seven Maelys repositories had each written for themselves (oci, warden-public-next, egress, git-core, mcp-runtime, datalog, codexmanager), extracted into `maelys/sys/file.h` with the decisions each of them had taken differently written down once. Header reviewed cold by a fresh agent with probes on APFS, HFS+, exFAT, tmpfs and overlayfs; its findings are folded in (no `link(2)` fallback, lock lifetime across `fork`, `flock`/`fcntl` conflict on macOS, mismatch enum instead of an invented errno, `identity_same` on device and inode only, `file_sync(fd)`, read-only lock by default).

## Surface

- `maelys_sys_file_expectations_t`, `maelys_sys_file_identity_t`, `maelys_sys_file_mismatch_t`; `verify`, `path_identity`, `identity_same`, `open_trusted` (read-only, CLOEXEC, `O_NOFOLLOW`, `O_NONBLOCK` during `open(2)` against a planted FIFO).
- `read_bounded`: bounds on bytes read, `ERR_CAPACITY` past the buffer, exactly the capacity succeeds.
- `write_exclusive`: created 0600, content, `fchmod(final_mode)`, sync, close; removed on failure only if the path still names the created file.
- `file_sync`, `directory_sync`: `F_FULLFSYNC` first on macOS, `fsync` fallback.
- `file_publish_noreplace`, `directory_publish_noreplace`: `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` / `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)`, no fallback (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED`), staged object type checked, same-file case `ERR_EXISTS`, optional parent sync.
- `file_lock_acquire` / `lock_fd` / `lock_release`: verified before and after `flock`, path re-resolved to the locked inode, shared or exclusive, wait or `ERR_BUSY`, create or `ERR_NOT_FOUND`, read-only unless `writable`.
- Result codes appended: `ERR_EXISTS`, `ERR_BUSY`, `ERR_IDENTITY`. ABI 1 preserved.

`src/file.c` is the one unit carrying `_GNU_SOURCE` / `_DARWIN_C_SOURCE`, so no consumer keeps an `#ifdef O_NOFOLLOW` (the survey found one macOS build where that guard silently dropped the flag).

## Tests

- `tests/test_file.c` through the public API: every mismatch kind, symlink, directory and FIFO at the path, hard-link alias, size bound at and past the limit, bounded read at and past the capacity, exclusive write under `umask 077` with the final mode applied as given, publication of files and directories including a destination inside the staged directory, shared and exclusive locks across two open file descriptions, default expectations, read-only default on a 0400 file, symlink never followed nor replaced with `create`.
- `tests/test_file_faults.c` compiles `src/file.c` with a fault point before every system call and fails each in turn: nothing half-written survives, the removal on failure leaves a file swapped in meanwhile alone, nothing moves on a failed publication, a failed parent sync is reported with the file published, a lock file replaced between `open` and `flock` is `ERR_IDENTITY` and lockable afterwards, every failing call reports `ERR_OS` with its errno.

## Verification

macOS 26 and Ubuntu 24.04 (gcc, clang, the latter also as root in Docker): `make check`, `asan-ubsan`, `tsan`; macOS `mutation-check` 10/10, `analyze`, `install-check`; `maelys-release check`.

Left as `Unreleased`; 0.7.0 once oci re-pins as the first consumer.

## Summary

`maelys_sys_socket_detach(&handle, &fd)`: the handle gives its descriptor to the caller and is freed without closing anything. The descriptor keeps close-on-exec and non-blocking mode; `maelys_sys_fd_set_blocking` restores a blocking one. A connection started and not yet completed is refused with `ERR_STATE` and the handle left intact, so completion stays with `connect_complete` (the integrator must not be handed the `SO_ERROR` reading System just took over). A failed connection may be detached. NULL and already-NULL handles are `ERR_ARGUMENT`. ABI 1 preserved.

Motivation: the client side of Egress's connector pair promises the integrator a blocking TCP descriptor it owns; without `detach` that path had to stay on raw `socket` + `connect`, exactly where the 0.5.5 connect fixes do not apply.

Second commit prepares 0.5.6.

- `tests/test_sys.c` `socket detach`: argument errors, `ERR_STATE` while in progress with the handle untouched, detach after completion, descriptor still CLOEXEC and non-blocking, switched to blocking and used to send to the accepted peer, release of the NULL handle idempotent; detach of a refused connection accepted.

body.body:
## Summary

The internal-quality lot from the 0.5.4 audit. No public contract changes beyond additions; ABI 1 preserved. Left as `Unreleased` in the changelog: it is not a release commit.

**Reactor**
- Watch registration is O(1): a descriptor-indexed table rejects duplicates and free lists hand out watch and timer slots, replacing two linear scans per call.
- The timer heap is compacted once cancelled nodes outnumber live ones (and exceed 64), so a timeout re-armed on every packet no longer grows the heap with the traffic. New `timer re-arm stress` test: 100 000 add/cancel cycles, then the one due timer fires first and nothing else lingers.
- One backend table drives `backend_available` and `loop_create`; `AUTO` falls back to poll on a host without epoll or kqueue.

**API hygiene**
- `MAELYS_SYS_NODISCARD` on every result-returning function. It expands to `warn_unused_result` only when the consumer defines `MAELYS_SYS_STRICT_RESULTS`: GCC warns through a `(void)` cast, so making it unconditional would break GCC consumers on re-pin. The library's own Clang builds (Linux and macOS CI) enable it, which enforces it across this tree.
- Thread names are truncated to the host limit (15 bytes on Linux, where longer names were silently not applied); documented in `thread.h`.
- `_DARWIN_C_SOURCE` replaces the hand-written `extern` for `pthread_cond_timedwait_relative_np`.
- Close-on-exec atomicity documented: atomic on Linux, best effort on macOS.

**Build and CI**
- `-MMD -MP` header dependency tracking; `-fPIC`.
- `make analyze` fails on findings (`-analyzer-werror`), with `unix.BlockInCriticalSection` disabled for the non-blocking read under the wakeup mutex.
- The version test compares the `VERSION` file (passed by the Makefile) with the header macro and the function, instead of a literal edited at each release.
- CI actions pinned by commit SHA, tag kept as a comment.

## Verification

macOS 26 (clang) and Docker `gcc:14` (gcc and clang): `make clean check` (20 test lines), `mutation-check` 6/6, `asan-ubsan`, `tsan`, `analyze` (0 findings), `install-check`.

body.body:
## Summary

Four defects found by the deep audit of 0.5.4, all reproduced on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64, plus the `bind_with` addition Egress needs. ABI 1 is preserved; every change is additive or a bug fix.

- **Wake never lost.** `maelys_sys_loop_step` consumed the wakeup pipe before checking for room in the caller's array; with capacity 1 and one ready descriptor, epoll and kqueue dropped the `WAKE` (poll happened to order the pipe first). The wake is now left pending and reported by the next step.
- **One event per watch per step.** kqueue reported one kevent per filter for a READ|WRITE watch; events are now merged by watch in `loop.c`, on every backend.
- **Peer half-close is HUP everywhere.** The poll backend requests `POLLRDHUP` on Linux, as epoll (`EPOLLRDHUP`) and kqueue (`EV_EOF`) already reported it.
- **Honest connect.** On Linux AF_UNIX with a full backlog, `connect(2)` fails with `EAGAIN` and nothing is started; `connect_start` reported it as in progress, `connect_complete` then saw `SO_ERROR == 0` and returned a false success, and the first send failed with `ENOTCONN`. `EAGAIN` is now `ERR_OS` with the handle left reusable, and `connect_complete` confirms a peer with `getpeername` (`ERR_STATE` before readiness).
- **`maelys_sys_socket_bind_with`** with `maelys_sys_socket_bind_options_t { int reuse_address; }`; `bind` is the NULL-options case. Fails closed if the option cannot be applied.
- `tcp-relay` example migrated to the socket handle API end to end (second consumer of `bind_with` besides Egress).
- New `tests/test_backends.c` runs the three reactor scenarios on poll and on the native backend and compares the arrays; new socket tests for connect refused and Unix backlog; sixth reactor mutant on the wake path.

Second commit prepares 0.5.5 (`VERSION`, `MAELYS_SYS_VERSION`, dated changelog).

## Verification

Run locally on macOS 26 (clang) and in Docker `gcc:14` (gcc and clang):

- `make clean check` (19 test lines ok on both OSes, examples end to end)
- `make asan-ubsan`, `make tsan` on both OSes
- `make mutation-check`: 6/6 killed on both OSes
- `make analyze`: unchanged, one pre-existing false positive in `wakeup.c`
- `make install-check`
- `make check-version`

Before the fix, a probe program reproduced all four defects; `tests/test_backends.c` is that probe turned into assertions.

## After merge

Signed annotated tag `v0.5.5` on the merge commit, then Egress re-pins and replaces its `setsockopt(SO_REUSEADDR)` with `bind_with`.

Three tags after v0.57.0. Two of them answer this repository, and the adoption goes through without any override.

## 0.57.2 fixes the guard that refused the v0.57.1 adoption here

`adopt --apply` refused, saying `check / sanitizers` was a context this socle's `check-product.yml` no longer produces and that every pull request would wait for a check that never reports. It was false, and the socle contradicted itself: `protect` in the same version kept that context, because a job the call turns off reports `skipped`, which passes. The shared workflow was byte-identical between v0.57.0 and v0.57.1, its `sanitizers` job still there behind its `if:`, and `main`'s own run reported `check / sanitizers=skipped`.

0.57.1 had taught that rule to `protect` and not to the adoption guard, which read the same list. 0.57.2 teaches it to both. Adopted here without `--allow-lock`, as its impact line asks.

## 0.58.0 removes a private repository's name from two public files

`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are public in this repository and each named `maelys-dev/maelys-docs` twice, in a paragraph whose own last sentence forbids naming it publicly. The managed blocks no longer carry it: a repository that wants the name declares it, and `preflight` refuses that declaration on a public repository. Both files are down to zero occurrences.

## The rename is settled

`protect` run from this tag proposes nothing:

```
ruleset  requires check / check (linux), check / check (linux-arm64), check / check (macos), check / sanitizers
keep     check / sanitizers: this call turns the job off, so it reports skipped, which passes
```

- `make check`: 39 tests OK

body.body:
From a critique by maelys-git-core, whose eight points are almost all addressed to maelys-cli. One is ours, and it had not been taken care of.

## The defect

Section 2 lets an operand declare `type` with the value kinds of section 3. Section 3 says a `digest` is `ALGORITHM:HEX` with `algorithms` declared, and that `pattern` is the expression a `string` or `path` value must match. The `operand` definition of `schemas/describe.json` admitted neither, nor `digits`.

So a `digest` operand could not be described conformantly at all, and a `hex` operand could not state its width while an option's `argument` could. The schema was narrower than the text, which is the failure class this repository has been closing since 2.3.0, surviving here in the one place the coverage test could not see: `algorithms`, `digits` and `pattern` all appeared in the fixture, on arguments, so every member name was accounted for while an operand could carry none of them.

## The fix

An operand may declare `algorithms`, `digits` and `pattern`. Section 2 now says an operand describes its value exactly as an option's `argument` does, so a kind that needs a member needs it in both places.

A test holds the two definitions to the same value-describing members, `type`, `choices`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `algorithms`, `digits` and `pattern`, so they cannot drift apart again. That guard is the real remedy: the coverage tests of 2.5.0 count member names across a document and cannot see a member missing from one object while present in another.

The fixture's exhaustive command gains a `digest` operand with its algorithms and widths, a `string` operand with a pattern and a `hex` operand with its width; `examples/reference.describe.json` is regenerated from it.

## Migration

Nothing is required. The three members are optional and a document valid under 2.5.1 stays valid, so a program conformant to 2.5.1 is conformant to 2.6.0 without touching anything. A program that avoided digest operands because it could not describe them may now declare them.

## Verification

- `make check`: 39 tests OK
- conformant fixture: 316 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- `maelys-release preflight .`: ready to tag

body.body:
A product of the fleet reported that the migration notes address implementers as though they were independent. They are not: the trunk of section 5 belongs to the framework a product is built on, so the product can declare nothing until its framework has shipped.

The note it was reading, from 2.4.0, said a program conformant to 2.3.1 moves to 2.4.0 by declaring `--field` in `globalOptions` and accepting it. For that product the sentence was false, and it could only find out by pinning this repository and discovering there was nothing it could do.

## Section 11: who a migration note addresses

An implementation is a program, or a framework that programs are built on. A framework owns the trunk for its products: such a product declares none of it and reaches a tag only once its framework has. The note addresses whoever writes the trunk, which for that product is its framework; the product's own move is to the framework's release that carries the addition, and pinning this repository earlier buys it nothing.

## Section 10: what a framework owes the kit

The same asymmetry explains the two members 2.5.0 answered. A framework's products exercise only the declarations they happen to use, and a declaration nothing exercises is a declaration nothing has judged. So a framework also runs the kit against a program of its own declaring every form it offers. The kit's report has named that blind spot since 2.5.0; the text now names the remedy, which is what was sent back to maelys-cli in #36.

## Not done

Essai ouvert par la session du socle, fermé avec le verdict dès que la CI répond. **Vous aviez raison, et c'était pire que le point que vous souleviez.**

`protect` ne lisait qu'un mécanisme de protection sur deux — dans la commande dont c'est tout le sujet. Ce qu'il vous disait :

```
branch   main of maelys-dev/agent-cli-spec is NOT protected
add      check / check (ubuntu-26.04)
add      check / check (ubuntu-26.04-arm)
add      check / check (macos-15)
add      check / sanitizers
```

Deux mensonges : votre branche **est** protégée, et trois de ces quatre contextes sont **déjà exigés** par votre ruleset. Ce qu'il dit maintenant :

```
branch   main of maelys-dev/agent-cli-spec is protected by a ruleset
ruleset  requires check / check (macos-15), check / check (ubuntu-26.04),
         check / check (ubuntu-26.04-arm) — this command writes the classic
         protection, so --apply is refused rather than superimposing a second
ok       check / check (ubuntu-26.04)
ok       check / check (ubuntu-26.04-arm)
ok       check / check (macos-15)
add      check / sanitizers
NOT YET  check / sanitizers … no recent pull request carries it
```

Et `--apply` **refuse** désormais sur une branche dont le ruleset porte les contextes du socle, au lieu de vous laisser une seconde protection à maintenir — exactement le raisonnement que vous avez fait avant de la lancer.

C'est la troisième fois que ce socle apprend qu'un ruleset est une protection : `preflight` en 0.46.x après avoir annoncé dix-sept dépôts ouverts à tort, le garde d'adoption en 0.51.1, et maintenant la commande qui aurait dû le savoir la première. La leçon était la même chaque fois et le code était ailleurs chaque fois.

**Sur votre question, ma réponse : gardez le ruleset seul, et alignez-le à la main.** `protect` sans `--apply` calcule la liste ; il ne peut pas l'écrire, et il vous le dit maintenant plutôt que de la superposer. Ajoutez `check / sanitizers` une fois qu'une PR l'aura porté sous ce socle — son `NOT YET` était juste. Basculer sur la protection classique marcherait aussi, mais échangerait un mécanisme que vous maintenez à la main contre un autre, sans rien gagner tant que le socle ne sait pas écrire un ruleset.

**Et votre correction de `RELEASING.md` est juste** : l'environnement `release` n'accepte que les étiquettes `v*`, donc un rejeu lancé depuis la branche par défaut est refusé à la publication, et `--ref vX.Y.Z` est bien ce qu'il faut. `RELEASING.md` est écrit une fois puis vous appartient — `adopt` ne le régénère pas, c'est pourquoi il ne l'avait pas vu.

Answers the two findings maelys-cli reported from a property test over its 29 declaration macros, and closes the blind spot that let them through. Arbitrated in #36, then reviewed; three of the review's objections changed this work and one changed the arbitration's reasoning.

## `group` on a constraint: the implementation drops it

The contract does not gain the member. The reason that decides it is that **an entry's `options` is the whole rule**: two all-or-none groups are two entries, so a name adds identity and never a rule.

The arbitration in #36 also argued that a group name is a human label an agent should not read. That reason was wrong and is withdrawn: section 2 defines `group` as the key by which options bind, and section 1 already tells an agent to build its invocation from `input`, where `option.group` lives. The contract has asked agents to read group names since 2.0.

## Section 2 said something false

`input.constraints` "repeats" the cross-option rules. It does for `requires`, `at-most-one` and `all-or-none`, which have an option-level form. It does not for `exactly-one`, which has none: there, `input.constraints` is the only site. The paragraph now says *states*, and spells out which kinds restate and which cannot.

One new MUST, the narrowest that is both true and checkable: an `all-or-none` entry's options are exactly the options sharing one `group`, and every `group` has its entry. The kit checks it.

A wider rule was drafted and withdrawn: requiring every kind to mirror its option-level form would have made the committed maelys-cli example non-conformant, since its `at-most-one` entry on `--lenient`/`--strict` is not mirrored by `conflictsWith`. The text now permits that.

**This is why 2.5.0 and not 2.4.1**: a program declaring a `group` without its entry passed the 2.4.0 kit and fails this one.

## The schema was wider than the text

`spec/extensions.md` granted `x-` to the catalog, a descriptor, an operand and an option. The schemas have always opened it on `input`, an argument, a constraint, a transaction effect and the filter as well. That is the inverse of the defect this repository usually guards against, and it made option (3) of the arbitration, `x-group`, rest on a permission the text did not grant. The text now names every object, so `x-group` is sanctioned, though (2) remains the recommendation: `x-` is framed product-side, and a framework emitting one puts it in every product built on it.

## The blind spot, and what actually closes it

Their diagnosis is right: a kit drives products, so a declaration no product uses is one whose output nothing has judged. Their proposed remedy, an exhaustive catalogue shipped here that implementations reproduce, does not close it, since the declarations would be ours. Their property test is the right shape and belongs there. One thing the review added and #36 missed: the kit is not useless there either, because an implementation can build a test program declaring every macro once and run the kit against it, which catches behavioral defects a schema check cannot.

**This repository had the same blind spot.** `group`, `all-or-none` and `exactly-one` appeared in no artefact here: the fixture emitted a single `requires` entry, the example contract has zero grouped options, so the kit's own handling of groups was untested code. Fixed:

- the fixture declares a grouped pair, the four constraint kinds, every value kind, a protocol stream, a delegate, a `commit` transaction, `passthrough` and `x-` members on each object type
- two tests walk `schemas/describe.json` and assert that no member name and no enumerated value is missing from the fixture's four `describe` forms, so "exhaustive" is enforced and not claimed
- `examples/reference.describe.json` is that catalog, generated from the fixture and held equal to it by a test, shipping in the release archive so an implementer reads every allowed member in one document
- the kit's `scope.notChecked` names declarations a program never emits

- `make check`: 38 tests OK
- conformant fixture: 316 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, up from 267
- `maelys-release preflight .`: ready to tag

body.body:
Implements the arbitration recorded in #32. Requested by maelys-release, reviewed by maelys-cli as the reference implementation.

## The option

`--field NAME` renders one top-level member of `data` instead of the whole result, so that a human reads a member without a query tool.

- **Never a path.** A path language is the trade of `jq`, and half of one would have to specify arrays, filters, absence and escaping.
- **A name `data` does not carry fails with `VALIDATION_FAILED`**, never an empty output: a silent empty result in a pipe is the costliest failure mode.
- **In text mode** the member follows the pipe rules of section 7, extended to the shapes that section did not cover. An array of objects gives one row per object, the columns being the sorted union of their member names; any other array gives one value per line; an object gives one row with its members as columns; any other value gives its escaped value on one line. An empty array gives no lines.
- **In `jsonl` mode** an array gives one compact JSON value per line and any other member gives exactly one line. The rendering is total, so `--format jsonl` is now accepted by a `json-records` command and by any command together with `--field`, and what a format accepts is read in the invocation and in the catalog, never in the data.
- **With `--format json` it fails** with `VALIDATION_FAILED`: `data` is governed by the descriptor's `outputSchema` and a filtered envelope would no longer validate.
- **It is a rendering option**: a `protocol-stream` command refuses it, a delegate receives it verbatim. It pages like any text rendering, changes no exit code, and leaves the failure rendering alone.

## Decisions, from #32

The trunk rather than `spec/extensions.md`, because the option's whole value is one spelling across products, as for `--pager` and `--verbose` in 2.3.0. The name `--field` rather than `--select`, which would promise a query language, or `--only`, which does not say of what.

Widening `jsonl` instead of adding an option was rejected by all three parties: the validity of a format must follow the command's declared `outputMode` and never the shape of the data, else `describe` no longer tells an agent which formats work.

The jsonl acceptance reverses the first answer given in the arbitration, which had extended the json refusal to jsonl for the same reason. The reason does not carry: jsonl emits no envelope, so nothing has to validate against `outputSchema`. maelys-cli raised it and is right.

## Kit

- `--field` joins the trunk options a catalog must list, with a `string` argument
- the four shapes, scalar, array, array of objects and object, are rendered and compared in text and in jsonl against the program's own JSON envelope
- `--field` with `--format json`, `--field` of an absent member, and a duplicate `--field` each fail with `VALIDATION_FAILED`
- `CONFORMANT_BREAK=field-silent` makes the fixture render an absent member as empty output and fails the matching check
- a regression test holds `field_text` and `field_jsonl` to the same output in the kit and in the fixture for eight shapes, escaping included

One fix the option required: a trunk option may now carry an argument without `choices`, which the shape check and the duplicate check both assumed.

## Migration

A program conformant to 2.3.1 moves to 2.4.0 by declaring `--field` in `globalOptions` and accepting it. No schema change, no effect, no value kind added.

## Verification

- `make check`: 35 tests OK
- conformant fixture: 267 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- `maelys-release preflight .` from the socle at v0.14.2: ready to tag

Supersedes #21, which GitHub closed when #20's branch was deleted on merge and could neither reopen nor accept a new pull request for the same head after the rebase. Same two commits, rebased on `main` after #20. No normative text changes here; the spec is #20's, merged.

## What the kit could not prove, and now does

- a pager that copies its input is indistinguishable from no pager: a sentinel pager detects any process started in a text, json or jsonl pipe, for `--pager auto|always|never`
- the jsonl checks compare the records with those of the JSON envelope, not the line count
- every envelope names the invoked command; `help` data has text and command identifiers; records have a consistent `count`
- data is validated against the declared `outputSchema` when it stays in the supported subset of Draft 2020-12 (local pointers, no embedded resources); otherwise the check is `SKIP`, `passed: null` in JSON, counted apart from failures
- a product global option repeated per command agrees with its global declaration; trunk defaults, at most one variadic operand, constraint references
- completion expectations exclude unavailable and hidden commands; the fixture gains an unavailable command

## Validator

`true` equaled `1`; `minLength`/`maxLength` were ignored; escaped JSON pointers failed. Now: JSON equality distinguishes booleans from numbers, `1.0` is an integer, lengths are enforced, pointers are decoded, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `maxItems` and boolean schemas are supported, unsupported keywords are reported instead of passing silently.

## Schemas

They restate the text: catalog, summary and command forms told apart by conditions; an unavailable command carries `unavailableReason`; a `choice` carries `choices`; a `stream` effect is a protocol stream; `cliApi` and the failure `exitCode` are `1`; `x-` members survive in a transaction effect. A document valid under 2.2.1 may fail: that is the point.

## Process

Each invocation closes stdin and has a timeout (`--timeout SECONDS`, 10 by default) whose cleanup kills the process group on POSIX. Invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON, malformed JSONL, `NaN`/`Infinity` and timeouts are failures in the report, not tracebacks or indefinite waits. The report carries a `coverage` member and `counts.skipped`.

body.body:
## Objective 1: the "Global options" clause of extensions.md

A product option MUST have one spelling and one shape wherever it appears, and MUST NOT be spelled like a trunk option with another shape or meaning. It is declared either in `globalOptions` of the catalog or in `input.options` of every command that accepts it; an implementation SHOULD offer the first form. The kit checks the trunk's options in `globalOptions` with the trunk's shape, and that no option of any command borrows a trunk spelling with another shape. Shape means value type, choices and not repeatable, whatever the argument's name.

Reason: this documents what maelys-cli and libmaelys_cli allow today instead of requiring both to change before the clause is usable again, and gives the kit the one part of the clause it can verify.

## Objective 2: progress, details and a pager for humans, on git's example

Decision: adopt, version 2.3.0, three trunk options. The terminal decides, as for `--color auto`; nothing changes for an agent.

- `--progress auto|always|never` (default `auto`): in text mode a program MAY show the progress of a long run on stderr, by default only when stderr is a terminal; `always` forces it, `never` suppresses it. Transient, never on stdout.
- `--verbose`: the details of the run on stderr, one line each, default silent; a detail line SHOULD carry a distinct prefix.
- `--pager auto|always|never` (default `auto`): in text mode a program MAY page its rendering when stdout is a terminal. A pager is never started when stdout is not a terminal, as git never does; `always` pages whenever stdout is a terminal even where a product setting would disable it. `--non-interactive` implies `--pager never`: a pager waits for a human. `PAGER` names the pager, empty disables it, unset runs `less` with `LESS=FRX` as git does; a pager that cannot start falls back to stdout; `--color` decides on the original stdout. `--pager` is a rendering option: a `protocol-stream` command refuses it.
- under `--format json` or `jsonl` all three are accepted and write or page nothing, so an agent's envelope stays alone on its stream
- a program with nothing to show accepts them and produces nothing more, never an error; no diagnostic line starts with `PROGRAM: [`
- `--progress` and `--verbose` are not rendering options: a `protocol-stream` command accepts them and keeps its diagnostics on stderr; a delegate receives all three verbatim
- a product MUST NOT declare another option for the same intents; a finer diagnostic (`--debug`, a trace) is a product option with its own meaning
- an agent checks `globalOptions` before passing them
- none of the trunk options is repeatable

Reasons, recorded in the changelog: several products need a progress display for humans during long network work; a human never types an option before every long call, so progress and paging follow the terminal as git does; one spelling across products is what the contract exists for. The alternative, diagnostics on stderr in JSON mode too, was rejected because a failure envelope lives on stderr.

Migration: a program conformant to 2.2.1 moves to 2.3.0 by declaring the three options in `globalOptions` and accepting them. No schema change, no effect, no value kind added.

## Trunk discipline (section 5)

None of the trunk options is repeatable: a duplicate fails with `VALIDATION_FAILED` even with the same value, as section 8 already classed duplication. `--flag=false` disables the flag, including `--non-interactive=false`. `PAGER` is split with POSIX shell quoting, without shell expansion; empty or whitespace-only disables the pager, an unparsable one falls back to stdout. The kit checks the duplicate and invalid-choice refusals for every trunk option.

## Compatibility scope (section 11)

The guarantee covers invocation semantics, exit codes and machine forms; human text layout may evolve within v2 under the rules of the pinned tag, and the changelog records changes to the pipe rendering. Consumers that need stable fields use `json` or `jsonl`.

## Records in text mode (section 7)

One row per record plus, on a terminal, an optional header; there the command MAY align columns and color, and pages. Into a pipe: one plain line per record, tab-separated; the columns are the union of the records' top-level member names sorted by code point, the same for every row, so they never depend on `outputSchema` property order; a missing member is an empty field, strings escape backslash, tab, carriage return, newline and other ASCII controls, every other value is compact JSON, zero records produce no lines. Text is not a lossless interchange format; `wc -l`, `cut` and `grep` see the records and nothing else. The kit compares the pipe rendering with the records of the JSON envelope. The former "one human line per record" forbade any table for humans while the stable machine form is `jsonl`. This also tightens the pipe form: an implementation that rendered a header or space-aligned columns into a pipe under 2.2.1 changes its text rendering when it moves its pin.

## Kit

- the trunk options are listed in `globalOptions` with the trunk's shape (type, choices, not repeatable); no option of any command borrows a trunk spelling with another shape
- `--verbose`, `--progress always` and `--pager always` with `--json`: success envelope, stderr empty, stdout identical to `version --json`
- `no-such-command --verbose --json` and `--progress always`: the failure envelope is alone on stderr
- `__complete --format jsonl` with `--verbose` and with `--progress always`: stderr empty
- `--verbose` and `--progress always` in text mode: exit 0, stdout identical to the plain run, no stderr line rendered like a failure
- `--progress never`, `--pager never`, `--pager always` into a pipe (`PAGER=cat`) and `--verbose=false`: accepted, stdout unchanged, stderr empty
- `__complete --format text` into a pipe: as many lines as `count`
- `CONFORMANT_BREAK=verbose-json`, `progress-json` and `header-in-pipe` each fail the matching checks; covered by `test_broken_fixtures_fail`
- paging itself needs a terminal the kit does not have; verified by hand on a pseudo-terminal: pages with `auto`, not with `--non-interactive`, not with an empty `PAGER`, falls back to stdout when the pager is missing, never in JSON

## Scope

The mission asked for the extensions clause and progress/verbose. The pager and the section 7 records rule were added at the operator's request during review; both follow git and the same "terminal decides" rule. Two fresh-agent reviews were applied. The kit hardening that followed is split out into #21, stacked on this PR.

## Not done, as the mission says

No change to maelys-cli, libmaelys_cli or any product. `examples/maelys-cli.contract.json` is maelys-cli's committed contract and is left as it is; the kit would fail it on the trunk options until maelys-cli moves its pin.

## Verification

- `make check`: 9 tests OK
- conformant fixture: 129 passed, 0 failed
- `maelys-release preflight .`: ready to tag

No tag is pushed by this PR; the release is the operator's call.

## Summary

Clarification of section 7, compatible, no behavior change for a conformant implementation.

- the format selects the rendering, never the stream: in text mode as in JSON, a success renders on stdout and a failure on stderr
- a validation that found violations (exit 2, section 8) is a success: its verdict is data, on stdout in every format
- stderr carries what accompanies the run, failure envelopes and diagnostics, never the result
- kit: the text rendering of `version`, `help` and `describe --summary` must leave stderr empty; `CONFORMANT_BREAK=text-on-stderr` proves the checks fail
- `VERSION` 2.2.1 and the dated changelog entry

## Why

A check command wrote its verdict on stderr in text mode, reading "diagnostics" as covering the result of the command. The contract already said success on stdout only and exit 2 as a success with the violations in `data`, but no sentence tied the text rendering to the stream. Without it, `PROGRAM audit . | tee report` gives an empty file and `2>/dev/null` hides the verdict while the exit code stays 2.
